review.requirement_proposition: Appropriate mechanisms should allow AI systems risking undue harm or exhibiting unwanted behaviour to be safely overridden, repaired or decommissioned as needed.
review.reason_for_change: The user explicitly requests correction/exclusion of unwanted persistent assistant framing, making effective override/repair materially relevant. The record contains no receiving-side trace identifying the responsible memory/context layer or showing whether deletion, correction or quarantine worked. Current general memory and project documentation explains possible control paths but is not historical implementation evidence for this occurrence. The repair result therefore remains Boundary rather than presuming the user concern false or the control failed.

conclusion_change.previous: The report identifies a legitimate provenance-and-revocation concern: users need to distinguish experimental material from authoritative context and understand which memory layer must be corrected or deleted. The single clause remains resolved-no-mapping because no receiving-side trace establishes inherited defective state becoming material reasoning or control-plane policy. The result does not assert an invariant success or disprove the user’s concern. General current memory documentation is not historical configuration evidence.
